blockers.title: NT-1, NT-2 and NT-6 are assigned to DR-G10 on a property G10 does not claim, does not test, and cannot acquire without a successor the artifact does not propose
blockers.finding: DR-G10's live row says, in full: Claim 'TS major 1 and Rust merged major 2 remain opaque, one-shot, fate-compatible subprotocols'; Platform matrix / harness 'named: harness.DR-G10.provider-conformance.ts-major-1 (D-086; not authored; not QUALIFIED). exact V1 goldens, D9/fault joins, no-reuse/process cleanup'; Required retained evidence 'byte/fate parity and lifetime results'. D-086's naming artifact, gate-harness-naming.v3 at b5236612, says what that harness executes: 'Named V2 runner over pinned goldens for the TypeScript major-1 provider.' Every one of those formulations describes parity over recorded exchanges plus lifetime behaviour. None of them describes refusing input that is outside the frame vocabulary. The three classes routed to G10 are exactly negative-path refusals: NT-1's input is 'a worker frame whose type is Finding or any type outside the existing closed worker-to-host vocabulary'; NT-2's is a closed payload 'with an added findings/finding/verdict/threshold/waiver member'; NT-6's is 'a constructible extra member or out-of-vocabulary frame carrying a D9 class, exit number, or HostTermination'. A goldens-parity runner exercises the exchanges in the corpus; nothing in G10's cell or in D-086's naming states that the corpus includes hostile or out-of-vocabulary fixtures, and the retained evidence G10 must produce is parity and lifetime results, not refusal outcomes. The artifact bridges that gap by writing a property into G10 that G10 does not state: its whyThisGate for NT-1 says 'G10's claim is opaque/closed subprotocol', and its whyNotG10 for NT-3 says 'G10 owns closed-frame opacity'. G10's claim says opaque. Opacity means the host does not inspect a subprotocol's internals; closure means out-of-vocabulary frames are refused. A host can treat a subprotocol as opaque and have no test whatever that it refuses an unknown frame — the two properties are independent, and only one of them is in the cell. NT-6 has the most support, since 'D9/fault joins' does appear in the harness cell, but the half NT-6 needs is refusal of a component-supplied D9 arriving on an out-of-vocabulary frame or extra member, which is the same closure property, not the host-side fault-to-D9 mapping the join names. Decisively, G10's own Threshold / waiver cell reads 'any semantic change needs successor'. Extending G10's coverage to closed-vocabulary refusal is a semantic change to what the gate claims, so G10's row itself prescribes the route — a G10 successor — and this artifact neither proposes one nor records it as owed.
blockers.whyBlocker: This is the artifact's central output for three of seven classes, and it is the named attack for this review. If accepted as drafted, DR-133's leftover would stand recorded as owned by a condition-4 gate that does not test it, which is false ownership at exactly the place D-056 gate 3 looks when a later SATISFIED cycle asks whether the remainder is named. The corpus has consistently treated a refusal or coverage claim that the cited instrument does not support as a blocker, not a wording problem.
blockers.repair: Pick one and say which. Either route NT-1, NT-2 and NT-6 to the proposed DR-133 admission harness alongside NT-3/4/5/7, which costs nothing this artifact has already claimed; or keep them at G10 and record, as owed work, a DR-G10 successor that adds the closed-vocabulary refusal property to G10's claim and negative fixtures to its harness, citing G10's own 'any semantic change needs successor' clause as the authority for that route. What the artifact may not do is assert present G10 ownership on the strength of a paraphrase that adds 'closed' to a claim that says 'opaque'.

blockers.title: The route the artifact specifies for NT-3, NT-4, NT-5 and NT-7 cannot produce what D-056 gate 3 requires, so the leftover it is closing stays structurally unclosable on its own terms
blockers.finding: The artifact's stated purpose is to say 'which existing condition-4 obligation owns each v3 NT, and which classes still need a later D-086 named harness', and for four classes it answers with harness.DR-133.provider-only-admission.preview. It then constrains that answer twice: 'doesNotAddANewDRGRow': true, and 'The later D-086 successor, if adopted, names an identifier only.' D-056's pinned turn-2 subject, gate 3, requires that 'Each such remainder is already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner.' Two things are missing and both are load-bearing. First, the obligation. D-086's naming scheme attaches every harness to a gate row: gate-harness-naming.v3 has 22 entries, all DR-G*, and zero harness identifiers outside the harness.DR-G* namespace. An identifier hung off DR-133 — a condition-2 architecture row, not a gate — with no DR-G* row added is not a condition-4 obligation; naming it changes nothing about condition 4. Second, the owner. Gate 3 says 'with an owner', and the artifact names no owner for the proposed harness, or for any class; the string 'owner' does not occur in it at all, while G10's row carries 'Protocol + semantic owners' in the cell the artifact declined to quote. So an identifier-only naming with no gate row and no owner leaves gate 3 exactly as unsatisfied after the proposed successor as before it. The artifact is candid that it does not close the leftover today — 'NT-3/4/5/7 still lack a named condition-4 obligation until the later D-086 successor lands' — but the successor it specifies is not capable of supplying one, so the sentence promises a closure the design cannot deliver.
blockers.whyBlocker: The four classes are a majority of the join, and this is the artifact's own forward path rather than an incidental remark. A leftover-design closure whose specified route cannot reach the gate it exists to reach does not advance DR-133; adopting it would put a dead route on the record as the plan.
blockers.repair: State the gate. Either identify an existing DR-G* row whose claim covers host-owned admission — relation-registry rejection, policy/verdict/threshold/waiver refusal, Coverage-domain sufficiency, and RequestId/ExecutionId allocation — and attach the four classes there with that row's owner, or say plainly that closure requires a new DR-G* row plus a named owner, which is a D-002 required-gate-set change and therefore its own decision, and record that as the owed act. Either way name the owner, since gate 3 requires one. I checked the 22 live gate claims and did not find one that clearly owns host-side fact/policy admission, so the second branch is the likelier honest answer.

shouldFix.title: The artifact quotes two of DR-G10's eight cells and omits the five that bear on whether the join works, including that G10 is HARD-BLOCKED
shouldFix.finding: g10Quoted reproduces the Claim and the Platform matrix / harness cells, both byte-exact. It does not reproduce, or mention anywhere, the other five: Required retained evidence 'byte/fate parity and lifetime results'; Owner 'Protocol + semantic owners'; Assurance stage now 'V1 IMPLEMENTABLE; V2 not QUALIFIED'; Threshold / waiver 'any semantic change needs successor'; and Status 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh'. Measured: the subject contains neither 'HARD-BLOCKED' nor 'selector' nor 'owner'. D-086's naming artifact adds that G10's selectorRefreshStanding is 'UNPINNED-OWED'. A reader of this artifact learns that three classes are parked at a named existing gate and is not told that the gate is hard-blocked with an unpinned selector, that its retained evidence is parity rather than refusal outcomes, that its owner is named in a cell the artifact could have carried into the join, or that its own waiver cell routes semantic changes to a successor. Selective quotation of the two cells that support the join, when three of the five omitted cells cut against it, is the part that makes this more than an editorial gap.
shouldFix.whyNotBlocker: The omissions do not by themselves make a false statement — everything the artifact does quote is exact — and the ownership defect they conceal is already charged at B1. Repairing this alone would not make the join correct.
shouldFix.repair: Quote the whole DR-G10 row, or at minimum add Status, Owner and Threshold / waiver to g10Quoted, and record G10's selectorRefreshStanding from gate-harness-naming.v3. Add an owner field to every class, since D-056 gate 3 requires one and the join is the artifact that should carry it.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. Thirteen attacks run, three landed. Custody is clean — subject a69926b6 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 2d1254e, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree — and D-142's application checks out, its D-056 insertion being exactly the 206 consented bytes. The artifact's hygiene is good and I want that on the record: all seven of v3's negative-test classes are carried with matching names, all three quoted cells are byte-exact against live file 08, both source digests reproduce, and the candidate framing is correct throughout. The content is where it fails. First, NT-1, NT-2 and NT-6 are parked at DR-G10 on a property G10 does not have. G10's claim is that the subprotocols 'remain opaque, one-shot, fate-compatible'; its harness is a goldens runner — D-086's own naming artifact says it executes a 'Named V2 runner over pinned goldens' — and its retained evidence is 'byte/fate parity and lifetime results'. The three classes routed there are negative-path refusals of out-of-vocabulary frames and extra members. The artifact bridges the gap by writing 'opaque/closed subprotocol' where the cell says opaque: opacity means the host does not inspect internals, closure means unknown frames are refused, and only the first is in the cell. G10's own Threshold / waiver cell settles the route — 'any semantic change needs successor' — and no G10 successor is proposed or recorded as owed. Second, the route for the other four classes cannot reach the gate it aims at. D-056 gate 3 requires the remainder be 'already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner'; the artifact proposes an identifier hung off DR-133 with doesNotAddANewDRGRow true and a successor that 'names an identifier only', and names no owner anywhere — the token 'owner' does not appear in the file at all. Every one of D-086's 22 named harnesses hangs off a DR-G* row, so an identifier attached to a condition-2 row is not a condition-4 obligation, and gate 3 stays exactly as unsatisfied after the proposed successor as before it. I checked all 22 live gate claims looking for a home for host-owned admission and found none, which means the honest answer is probably that closure needs a new DR-G* row and an owner — a D-002 required-gate-set change, and therefore its own decision. The SHOULD-FIX is that the artifact quotes two of DR-G10's eight cells and omits the five that bear on the join, including Status 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh', Owner, and the waiver cell that routes semantic changes to a successor; three of the five omitted cells cut against the join, which is what makes the selection more than editorial. A v2 that reassigns NT-1/2/6, names the gate and owner for the rest or says a new DR-G* row is required, and quotes G10's row whole would keep everything listed under whatSurvives.
